endorsements.quote: Performance metrics are generated using a held-out testing data set that is not used for model training, fine-tuning, or prompt iteration, is representative of the target population, and is sufficiently large to ensure statistical reliability.

First, the approach of evaluating variable-level performance metrics can be extended to assess model bias by stratifying metrics by demographic subgroups (eg, race/ethnicity, age, and sex), clinical subgroups (eg, by treatment, biomarker status, and stage), or even practice-level subgroups (eg, practice type, EHR type, and institution).

Each significant change to models or data delivery pipelines may necessitate rerunning quality assessment analyses to ensure consistent performance, creating an ongoing maintenance burden that must be factored into operational planning.

Although high-criticality, complex variables such as the one in the case study warrant rigorous, resource-heavy approaches (eg, subgroup analysis), variables with low criticality (ie, nonintervention, outcome, or cohort selection variables), with consistent documentation across subgroups or with high performance metrics, may allow for less intensive validation (eg, no subgroup analysis, skipping human performance benchmarks, and limiting number of validation assessments aside from metrics).

unlisted_practices: Assess LLM-extracted clinical data using verification checks for conformance, plausibility, and internal consistency at patient and cohort levels.
Benchmark LLM extraction performance against expert human abstraction using a common reference standard and report relative performance differences.
Run replication and benchmarking analyses comparing analyses on LLM-extracted data with human-abstracted datasets or external standards, in broad cohorts and subcohorts of interest.
Involve clinicians, research scientists, health equity experts, and engineers in a multidisciplinary team to design and interpret LLM data quality assessments.
Evaluate LLM extraction against local abstraction metrics and adapt verification checks and reference standards to local documentation and care patterns.

screen.reason: The paper proposes a framework (VALID) for evaluating and assuring the quality and reliability of clinical data extracted from electronic health records by large language models.
